passage: Every evening after homework, Kunal stood at his window in the Kolkata flat and tossed a rolled-up sock into his open laundry basket. He kept missing. Last night he told his friend Samir on the phone, “I'm going to practise basketball every day for a month.” Samir said, “Every day? Isn't that a lot?” Kunal thought and changed it. “Okay, I'll shoot ten times after homework, every day this week.” The next evening he counted ten throws. He made three, and grinned. He pinned a small card on his wall, wrote “Ten throws,” and ticked the first box.

qa.q: How many throws did Kunal plan each evening?
What did Kunal feel about his plan after Samir asked if it was a lot?
qa.a: He thought again and decided his big declaration was too much, so he chose a smaller plan he could actually keep.

qa.q: Why is Kunal's second plan more likely to work?
qa.a: It is small and specific, ten throws after homework for one week, and he made a card to tick it off.

qa.q: How might Samir have felt when Kunal changed the plan?
qa.a: He probably felt glad that his question helped, and maybe a bit proud of his friend.

grounding: A child declares an intention and revises it into a small, specific plan, which is more likely to succeed.

passage: “I am going to learn the whole tabla in one week,” Nikita announced at the dinner table. Her father raised an eyebrow. “The whole thing?” “Yes! Every day, for hours!” Gautam, her cousin, laughed. “You said that about the drawing, too.” Nikita frowned. “That time I forgot.” After a pause she said, “Okay, maybe I'll practise ten minutes after dinner, and learn the first beat by Sunday.” Her father nodded. “That sounds like something you can do.” Nikita wrote “ten minutes, first beat” on her hand with a pen, and grinned at Gautam.

qa.q: How many minutes did Nikita decide to practise?
What made Nikita change her declaration?
qa.a: Her cousin's remark about the drawing, and her father's raised eyebrow, made her realise the first plan was too big, so she chose a smaller step.

qa.q: Why did her father say the new plan sounds doable?
qa.a: It is small and specific, ten minutes after dinner and the first beat by Sunday.

qa.q: How might Gautam have felt about reminding Nikita of the drawing?
qa.a: He may have felt a bit teasing but also caring, since her new plan showed she listened. 🙂

grounding: A child declares I am going to learn everything and then reshapes it into a small, specific plan.
